[Sat 2026-05-09 04:57 UTC] Find a way to transmit the large archive file over the network.

A few practical options—pick what fits your environment/security constraints:

## 1) HTTP download link (quick, if you can expose a port)
On the machine that has the file:
```bash
cd /root/.openclaw
python3 -m http.server 8000 --bind 0.0.0.0
```
Then from the receiving machine:
```bash
curl -LO http://<sender-ip>:8000/workspace-project-with-git.tar.gz
```
Notes: open firewall/security group for TCP/8000; prefer doing this only on a trusted network.

## 2) SCP over SSH (standard, encrypted)
From the receiving machine:
```bash
scp root@<sender-ip>:/root/.openclaw/workspace-project-with-git.tar.gz .
```
If you need a non-root user, adjust path/permissions.

## 3) rsync over SSH (resumable, good for truly large files)
```bash
rsync -avP -e ssh root@<sender-ip>:/root/.openclaw/workspace-project-with-git.tar.gz .
```

## 4) Upload to object storage (S3/GCS/etc.) (best for sharing)
Example with AWS CLI:
```bash
aws s3 cp /root/.openclaw/workspace-project-with-git.tar.gz s3://YOURBUCKET/path/
aws s3 presign s3://YOURBUCKET/path/workspace-project-with-git.tar.gz --expires-in 86400
```

## 5) If you can only copy text: split + base64 (last resort)
```bash
split -b 50m /root/.openclaw/workspace-project-with-git.tar.gz part-
# transmit parts, then:
cat part-* > workspace-project-with-git.tar.gz
```
